subject: strandbeest
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: wind-walking beach creature of tubes.
Style: Theo Jansen kinetic sculpture.

spec.name: Strandwalker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen-style wind-walking beach creature built from pale PVC tube trusses, with a flapping spine wing, a wind-eating bow and two rows of linked legs striding the sand.
spec.layout: A long horizontal tube-truss spine runs the full 6.2 m from nose at z=+3.0 to tail at z=-3.0, riding 0.95 m above the beach on two parallel trains of walking legs (left legs at x≈+1.05, right at x≈-1.05), three legs per side spread along z from +2.4 to -2.4; each leg is the classic Strandbeest linkage — a triangle of rigid tubes from hip, a knee knuckle, a long lower shank and a flat paddle foot, feet flat on y=0. On top of the spine amidships sits a single great wing: a thin spar frame 2.2 m wide across x, rising to y=2.1, cloth panels stretched between tubes, hinged to flap. The bow at the front is the creature's mouth: a fan of short open tubes angled into the wind with a small red crank hub. The stern carries a bundle of wind-stomach bottles and one tall tail fin of stretched sail cloth. The style shows everywhere as skeletal tube frames: every member is a thin cylinder or slim box truss, every connection is a visible dark joint cuff or red pivot hub, pale canvas panels glow against the tubes, and nothing is skinned — the machine reads as bone and ligament from every angle. Front view: bow tubes flared, wing spreading left-right above, legs descending in a forest of thin tubes to paddle feet. The lowest points (the feet) touch y=0.

parts.builds: The full-length tube truss spine from nose to tail: a horizontal ladder of paired top and bottom chord tubes along z (top chord at y=1.55, bottom at y=1.15) joined by diagonal zig-zag web tubes and dark joint cuffs at every node, cross-braced triangles so the frame reads skeletal from every side. At the bow (z=+2.7..+3.05) the spine flares into the wind mouth: a fan of 9 short open tubes angled up and outward into the wind, ringed by a red crank hub disc, with a small mesh screen grille of thin crossed tubes. Mid-spine carries a row of small red pivot hubs on both sides at the hip mounts, plus a few tiny tube stubs and a hanging thin sensor antenna tube near the front. Colours: main chords in tube, diagonals in tubeShade, all cuffs and node blocks in jointDark, crank and hub details in crankRed, the antenna tip in crankRed.
parts.attaches: Roots at spineCenter and runs through spineF, spineB and nose joints; hands the hip sockets on hipLineL/hipLineR to the leg trains, the wingRoot platform to wingMast, noseMount to itself (bow ends there), and tailMount to the stern.

parts.builds: The great flapping wing above the spine: a central mast tube rising from the spine at wingRoot to y=2.05, carrying a horizontal main spar 2.2 m across x (from x=-1.1 to x=+1.1), with a lighter secondary spar behind it and thin rib tubes connecting them into four bays. Stretched between the spars are sail-cloth panels (thin flat slabs) in sail with darker sailEdge trim strips along the leading edge and a small red pennant flag at the left wingtip. Dark joint cuffs sit at the spar-mast crossings and at the wingHinge pivot; a small red crank arm connects mast to spine so the wing reads as wind-driven. The whole wing is tilted a few degrees and built to be flappable about the hinge.
parts.attaches: Roots on the spine's top chord at mount wingRoot and the joint wingHinge; meets spineCore only there, nothing below y=1.8.

parts.builds: The left row of three walking legs at x≈+1.05, one per hip joint (hipFL z=+1.9, hipFM z=+0.6, hipFB z=-0.7). Each leg is the Strandbeest linkage built from tubes: a short hip crank tube leaving the socket with a red pivot hub, a triangular rigid frame of three tubes down to a knee knuckle (dark joint cuff), a long lower shank tube angling down and forward, and a lower-joint cuff from which a flat paddle foot (a thin slab, 0.34 long × 0.16 wide) lands flat on y=0. A thin diagonal stay tube ties the leg frame back to a mid point so the triangle silhouette is unmistakable. All three legs are identical but phase-staggered slightly. Additional knee/shank joints are created inside this part parented to its hip. Colours: tubes and shanks in tube, diagonal stays in tubeShade, all knuckles, cuffs and hubs in jointDark, pivot hubs and foot edge strips in crankRed, paddle foot top in sail.
parts.attaches: One leg socket per hip joint (hipFL, hipFM, hipFB) at mount hipLineL; upper crank ends meet the spineCore side hubs; feet land flat on the floor.

parts.builds: The mirror of legTrainL on the right at x≈-1.05: three identical Strandbeest linkage legs on hipFR (z=+1.9), hipMR (z=+0.6), hipBR (z=-0.7), each with hip crank and red pivot hub, triangular tube frame to a dark knee knuckle, long lower shank, and a flat paddle foot landing on y=0, with a thin diagonal stay tube. Phase-staggered differently from the left row so the gait reads. Colours exactly as the left train: tube, tubeShade, jointDark, crankRed, sail foot tops.
parts.attaches: One leg socket per hip joint (hipFR, hipMR, hipBR) at mount hipLineR; upper crank ends meet the spineCore side hubs; feet land flat on the floor.

parts.builds: The tail assembly behind z=-2.7: a short horizontal tail boom of two tubes leaving the tailMount, then the wind-stomach — a tight bundle of 6 rounded bottles (capsules) in bottleTeal strapped to a small frame with dark straps and one red valve cap on the top bottle — plus a tall triangular tail fin of stretched sail cloth rising from the boom tip to y=2.0, panelled in sail with a sailEdge border and two thin batten tubes across it. The boom ends in a small dark tail knob. Colours: boom tubes in tube, frame in spineDark, straps and knob in jointDark, bottles in bottleTeal, valve in crankRed, fin in sail and sailEdge.
parts.attaches: Roots on the spine end at mount tailMount on joint tailRoot; overlaps spineCore only at the boom root z=-2.55..-2.7.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec for a wind-walking beach creature in Theo Jansen style — a Strandbeest. Tubes, wind sails, walking legs. Category: Abstract, made of tubes.

Model: ~2.4m wide, ~2.1m tall, ~6.2m long? Actually a strandbeest walks along... front faces +Z, so the creature's walking direction is +Z. Legs along the sides, wind wing/sail on top.

Plan the parts (3–6):
1. spine/body core — horizontal tube frame spine with triangular bracing, nose/bowsprit, wind organ tubes (glowing? no, beach creature — maybe wing on top).
2. wing — top sail/awning flapping, pump wing.
3. leg frame left and right — the famous leg linkage: many tube segments per leg, feet. Could be one part "legGearL" and one "legGearR" but symmetric parts split evenly; maybe one part builds both sides via mirror? The spec says each part is self-contained; builders can mirror. Let's do: leftLegs, rightLegs as two parts (4 legs each side? Strandbeests have many legs per side). Or one part "legs" building all legs might be too big. Split: "legTrainL" and "legTrainR", each budget ~200.
4. tail/stern: wind stomach — PVC bottle array / sail tail, plus ground props? Brief says only subject. Tail part: rear frame, sail fin, pump bottles.

So parts: spineCore (budget 200), wingMast (150), legTrainL (200), legTrainR (200), stern (150). Total 900. Good — 5 parts.

Joints: root at spine center, spine joints along length, wing hinges, hip joints per leg, knee joints... The joints array defines skeleton before parts run; both leg parts reference hipL1 etc. But legs per side: strandbeests have legs in a row. Let's simplify: 3 legs per side, each with hip joint. Actually the front part of a strandbeest has one leg assembly per side driving many feet. For abstract: give each side a leg chain per foot? Simpler: per side 3 hips, each hip joint, plus knee per leg. That's a lot of joints in the spec. The spec joints are just top-level named ones; the builder may create more? Actually spec says "joints is the skeleton, created in this order before any part runs". Parts list joints their geometry rides. Builders probably create more joints via chain in their own part. To be safe, define main joints: root, spine segments, wingRoot, wingTip, hips per side, tail. Let the leg part builders create leg linkage joints themselves (they'd use b.joint with parents named). Hmm, risky but acceptable — parts can create additional joints parented to listed ones.

Mounts: spineNose [0,1.5,2.6], spineTail [0,1.5,-2.6], wingRoot [0,2.0,0.3], hipLineL x=+1.0, etc.

Palette: PVC yellow-white tubes (#e8dcc0), dark joints (#33383f), red accents (#c8452a), sail (#d9cfae), sand amber, sea foam trim.

Keep it tight. Sizes: width 2.4, height 2.1, length 6.2 (legs extend in z along length? Strandbeest is long: many legs along length). Yes legs spread along z from 2.8 to -2.8.

Joints list:
- root "spine0" at [0,1.5,0], dir [0,0,1], role spine.
- spine1 [0,1.5,1.5], spine2 [0,1.5,-1.5], neck/ bow "nose" [0,1.6,2.6], "tailRoot" [0,1.5,-2.8] role tail.
- "wingHinge" at [0,1.9,0.4], parent spine0, dir [0,0,1]? wing flaps about x-axis: hinge line along X. joint dir [1,0,0] role hinge. 
- hips: hipFL at [1.05,1.2,1.9], hipFM [1.05,1.2,0.6], hipFB [1.05,1.2,-0.7]? And mirrored right x=-1.05. Roles "leg". Give parent spine0/spine1.
That's ~11 joints fine.

Mounts: spineCenter [0,1.5,0], noseMount [0,1.55,2.6], tailMount [0,1.5,-2.8], wingRoot [0,1.95,0.4], axleL... hipSockets are joints already. Also footline? feet rest on floor: legs own floor:true.

Floor: legTrainL and legTrainR floor true. Spine rests above y ~0.9 min.

Boxes:
- spineCore: [[-0.5,0.9,-3.0],[0.5,1.9,3.1]]
- wingMast: [[-1.1,1.85,0.2],[1.1,2.1,1.4]] — wing spans wide: maybe [[-1.15,1.85,0.1],[1.15,2.1,1.5]]. Wing is a long horizontal wing along X that flaps — like Strandbeest wings. Yes.
- legTrainL: [[0.3,0,2.6],[1.25,1.45,-2.6]]
- legTrainR mirrored.
- stern: [[-0.6,1.0,-3.2],[0.6,2.0,-2.6]] — hmm tail sail should be tall: [[-0.7,0.95,-3.25],[0.7,2.0,-2.55]]. Stern includes wind-stomach bottles and a tail fin sail rising to 2.0.

Actually the nose part: front bow with wind organ / mouth that eats wind. spineCore covers full length including nose.

Budgets: spineCore 200, wingMast 150, legTrainL 220, legTrainR 220, stern 110 = 900.

Write layout text describing style: pale PVC tubes, dark joint cuffs, red crank hubs, sail cloth.
